title: History 2: Variational autoencoders and the latent idea (2013)

questions.q: What is the gap between log p(x) and the lower bound L of the 2013 paper?
options: KL( q(z|x) ‖ p(z|x) ), the divergence from the true posterior
KL( q(z|x) ‖ p(z) ), the divergence from the prior
The reconstruction error of the decoder
Zero, whenever the decoder is Gaussian
questions.answer: KL( q(z|x) ‖ p(z|x) ), the divergence from the true posterior
questions.why: log p(x) = L + KL( q(z|x) ‖ p(z|x) ). In the lab the gap equals this KL in every row (0.7650 for the q shifted by 0.3) and is 0.0000 when q is the true posterior.

questions.q: The paper replaces the naive Monte Carlo gradient estimator with the reparameterised one. What is wrong with the naive one?
options: It averages to the right gradient but has very high variance
It is biased towards the prior
It cannot be computed unless z is discrete
It needs the true posterior in closed form
questions.answer: It averages to the right gradient but has very high variance
questions.why: The paper says the estimator "exhibits very high variance". In the lab both estimators average to the exact −5.1000, but the score-function one has 4.2 to 238.6 times the variance.

questions.q: In the lab, the encoder that may use x ends with a mean gap of 0.0002 nats and the one that ignores x with 7.9758. Why?
options: The true posterior mean moves with x, so a single fixed q cannot match it
The second encoder was trained for fewer steps
The second encoder used a different prior
Using x makes the decoder deterministic
questions.answer: The true posterior mean moves with x, so a single fixed q cannot match it
questions.why: The posterior mean is 2(x−1)/4.25. One function of x, trained only by the reparameterised bound, recovers it; this is the amortised recognition model of the paper.

questions.q: What does ComfyUI's VAE Encode return for an AutoencoderKL VAE such as the one in SD 1.x?
options: The mean of q(z|x); the log-variance half is computed and dropped
A fresh sample, mean + std times noise, on every run
The log-variance channels
The prior N(0, I)
questions.answer: The mean of q(z|x); the log-variance half is computed and dropped
questions.why: DiagonalGaussianRegularizer is built with sample=False, so its forward returns posterior.mode(), which is the mean. The sample() method exists but this path does not call it.

questions.q: In the lab a decoder trained on squared error faces two equally likely sharp images. What does its best output look like?
options: The average of the two, with a 0.50 plateau where they disagree
One of the two images, chosen at random
The sharper of the two images
Pure noise
questions.answer: The average of the two, with a 0.50 plateau where they disagree
questions.why: The best output has expected squared error 0.75, against 1.50 for a sharp image picked at random. Its largest jump between neighbouring pixels is 0.50, where either real image has 1.00.

questions.q: You shift q away from the true posterior. What happens to log p(x), the bound and the gap?
options: log p(x) stays, the bound falls and the gap grows by the same amount
All three fall together
log p(x) falls and the gap stays
The bound rises because q is more spread out
questions.answer: log p(x) stays, the bound falls and the gap grows by the same amount
questions.why: log p(x) doesn't depend on q. The identity splits it into the bound plus the KL to the posterior, so what one loses the other gains.
